candidateDecisions.label: Health pillar: nutrition, human biology and public health
Behaviour pillar: food choice, consumer behaviour and decision-making
Responsible innovation pillar: sustainable food innovation, markets and entrepreneurship
Food policy and regulation for health and sustainability

analysis: The closest option links sustainable farming, climate, conservation and life-cycle assessment with biochemistry and physiology, consumer behaviour, empirical research and sustainable business decisions. Entrepreneurship and consumer product design support responsible innovation, while governance and public economics connect to policy and incentives. The first-year-only planning cell for Research in a Sustainable Delta cannot support the advanced progression after methods. Qualitative Research Methodology supplies a sequenced team research process from design to evidence gathering and interpretation. It provides partial overlap with the applied researcher project but has a qualitative rather than R-based focus. The biomedical option builds from gateways, chemistry and physiology to lab practice, epidemiology, disease, pharmacology and systematic review. It responds to the health pillar through human biology and population research, with food systems represented by farming and environmental health contexts. The behavioural option builds from cognition and social psychology to economic decisions, health behaviour, persuasion, climate communication and market inquiry. It contributes evidence about consumer behaviour, not a specialist psychology-of-eating or nutrition sequence. Responsible innovation and regulation remain distinct reasonable emphases under the three-option limit. The strongest direct food-system overlap comes from sustainable farming and food-related environmental impacts, with broader physiology, biochemistry and behaviour courses supplying transferable foundations. No selected plan supplies dedicated nutrition, food-processing, food-safety or sensory science coursework.

alignment.rationale: Both develop academic inquiry, including evaluating sources and framing research questions. UCR also covers personal development and community engagement.
Both develop research design and measurement. UCR also teaches descriptive and inferential statistics in this course.
Both examine evidence and the reliability of claims. UCR focuses on misinformation and misleading reasoning, while Venlo examines how knowledge and evidence inform decisions under uncertainty.
Both develop team research and the reporting of findings. UCR focuses on qualitative research. Venlo completes a linked research sequence with data analysis in R, an article and a poster.
Both develop data analysis skills. Venlo collects and analyses data within an ongoing group project, while UCR studies experimental design and multivariate statistics.
Venlo begins a supervised research project with a group proposal. UCR develops research planning within methods courses.
Venlo’s final-year Portfolio follows development across the degree. UCR’s Personal & Professional Development course is taken in Year 1.
Both examine how the body functions, including digestion and metabolism. Venlo gives greater attention to nutrition and macronutrients.
Both examine judgement, incentives and biases. Venlo applies the material to questions of food choice, health and sustainability.
Both examine sustainability challenges and connections between society and environmental change. UCR focuses on climate drivers, impacts and responses.
Both take a whole-system view of environmental effects. UCR uses life-cycle assessment, while Venlo models interactions within food systems.
The example uses 15 EC outside a single concentration, including humanities and the alternate concentration. Interdisciplinary curricula instead require 10 EC of humanities.
The example uses 75 EC of concentration courses. The concentration requires at least 20 EC of advanced coursework and allows at most 20 EC of introductory coursework.
Choose five intermediate or advanced skills trainings.
Choose three concentration projects, including at least one advanced project.
